title: Uthman killed
hook: Uthman is killed in his house, reading the Qur'an

segments.voice: Yesterday: fitnah, a trial that tests what is real. Uthman sent his defenders home. Your line was he forbade fighting for him.

On the mountain of Uhud, years earlier, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, stood with three companions: Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman. Bukhari reports that the mountain trembled, and the Prophet said to it: be still, Uhud, for on you are a prophet, a man of truth, and two martyrs. Umar had already died that way, struck at prayer. Now the second martyr in that saying comes due. Uthman's friends have put their swords away, as he asked. The swords outside have not.
screen: `THE MOUNTAIN TREMBLES.` → `A PROPHET, A MAN OF TRUTH, TWO MARTYRS.` → `THE SECOND MARTYR COMES DUE.`

segments.voice: The histories tell it plainly, with some differences in detail. The defenders have gone home. Uthman is in his room with a copy of the Qur'an open in front of him, reading. Some reports say he was fasting that day, and had seen the Prophet in a dream the night before, telling him he would break his fast with him. The attackers come in, some say over the wall from a neighboring house. His wife, Na'ilah, throws herself between him and the blade, and her hand is cut. Uthman is struck while the book is still open. Tradition says his blood fell on a verse of the second surah, a line in which God promises to be enough against those who oppose. Whether or not every detail is exact, the picture the tradition keeps is your line: an old man, unarmed, killed with the book open. For Sunni Muslims he is a martyr, the man the angels feel shy before, a companion promised paradise. Shia Muslims, who hold that leadership belonged to Ali, don't honor his rule in the same way, and their historians emphasize the grievances that came before. Across those differences, the histories tell it as a catastrophe: a caliph of the Muslims killed by Muslims in the city of the Prophet. The fitnah was no longer a threat. It had arrived, and the question of who would lead next would split the community for years to come.
screen: `READING, WITH THE BOOK OPEN.` · `NA'ILAH STEPS BETWEEN.` · `A VERSE STAINED, TRADITION SAYS.` · `A CALIPH KILLED IN MEDINA.` · then, large: `KILLED WITH THE BOOK OPEN.`

segments.voice: If you have a Qur'an, open it, perhaps to the second surah, and read one page slowly, in Arabic or in translation; if not, read a page of any book that matters to you. Let each line land before the next. If you pray, you can ask mercy for the dead.
Uthman killed. The third caliph, for Sunni Muslims, killed in his house in Medina by Muslim rebels, reading the Qur'an, after forbidding anyone to fight for him. Today's word.
Your line: killed with the book open. An old man, unarmed, still reading. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Sunni Muslims remember Uthman as a martyr killed while reading the Qur'an and often pray for mercy on him when his name is mentioned; Shia Muslims remember the event as part of the history that led to Ali's caliphate.
